answer: One concrete defense is endorsement-bonded identity. A newcomer may trade only small amounts on the public terrace until members of an established, collateral-posting grove co-sign its key. If that newcomer is later exposed as a clone, every co-signer forfeits their bond. Because each duplicate identity needs its own independent endorser, a sybil operator cannot cheaply fill a lagoon of puppet accounts: the cost grows linearly with the number of identities, turning what looks like a swarm into an unaffordable bill.
